answer: Counterparty diversity, capped at the source. A key earns settlement rights after trading with four unrelated members this epoch, and each established member may sponsor at most three newcomers. A farm cannot close its own loop, so it must pay outsiders, whose quota is finite and whose standing drops when a sponsored key defaults. The ledger records pairings, so a graph pass flags cliques. New capital gets one visible inlet; identity gets narrow channels. Escrow receipts are sealed in quartz-hard multisig and re-signed each epoch, and a cedar-rooted registry keeps the sponsorship tree public.
